title: Two finite ordered Cech comparisons for a flasque resolution
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $F$ a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $e:F[0]\to G^\bullet$ a quasi-isomorphism of nonnegative cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose each $G^q$ has flasque underlying abelian sheaf [def-sc-zariski-flasque]. Let $(V_i)_{0\leq i<r}$ be a finite open cover of $X$, allowing $r=0$ when $X$ is empty. For each nonempty subset $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,r-1\}$ put $V_S=\bigcap_{i\in S}V_i$, and suppose the section augmentation $\Gamma(V_S,F)[0]\to\Gamma(V_S,G^\bullet)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. For $p,q\geq0$ define $L^p=\prod_{|S|=p+1}\Gamma(V_S,F)$ with the alternating restriction differential. Define the commuting double complex $D^{p,q}=\prod_{|S|=p+1}\Gamma(V_S,G^q)$, with horizontal alternating restriction differential and vertical resolution differential, with all terms zero outside $p,q\geq0$, and total differential $d_h+(-1)^p d_v$ [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Then the two cochain maps $\alpha:\Gamma(X,G^\bullet)\to\operatorname{Tot}(D)$ and $\beta:L^\bullet\to\operatorname{Tot}(D)$ are quasi-isomorphisms, where $\alpha$ is restriction into the $p=0$ summands and $\beta$ is the section map of $e$ into the $q=0$ summands. Their degree-zero composites with $\Gamma(X,F)\to\Gamma(X,G^0)$ and with $\Gamma(X,F)\to L^0$ agree. These component-defined maps commute with coefficient maps, restriction to open subsets carrying the restricted cover, and a scheme morphism $h:Y\to X$ with the inverse-image indexed cover $h^{-1}V_i$, whenever supplied $\mathcal O_X$-linear coefficient and cochain resolution maps $F\to h_*F'$ and $G^\bullet\to h_*G'^\bullet$ commute with augmentations (where $F'$ and $G'^\bullet$ are the coefficient sheaf and resolution on $Y$). The quasi-isomorphism assertion on $Y$ assumes the same flasqueness and section-augmentation hypotheses there. No flatness of $h$ is assumed.
